fs16.intro: Every current role carries one of three labels: Growing, Changing or Stable. The criteria and thresholds are published here, and past years' labels are kept so anyone can check whether a label held up.

meaning.growing: Demand for the skills this role needs is projected to grow and to outrun the people who hold them. Good moment to move in.
meaning.changing: The role's 2030 profile adds or raises a large share of its requirements. Plan your learning now; the work is being redesigned, not removed.
meaning.stable: Neither the demand signal nor the profile-change signal crosses its threshold.

fs16.howDesc: Criteria version {v}, in force from {year}. The first rule that matches decides the label.
fs16.firstMatch: Rules are checked in this order. Components are percentages from the released skills outlook and the role profiles; no staffing numbers are ever used or shown.

rule.changing: The 2030 role profile adds or raises at least {pct} of today's requirement weight.
rule.growing: Projected demand for the role's skill families grows by at least {pct} to {year}, and demand stays above the people who hold those skills.

basis.change: FS05 role profiles: new requirements count their full level, raised ones the increase, weighted core 3, important 2, useful 1
basis.growth: Released skills outlook (SIMULATED), skill families weighted by how much the role needs them; the 5% line follows O*NET Bright Outlook
basis.shortfall: Pressure, kept apart from later demand: projected demand minus holders, as a share of demand

fs16.lineStaff: Median demand growth across labelled roles
fs16.rolesDescPublic: Every current role and its label for each year. Past labels stay as they were published.
fs16.rolesDescStaff: Every current role, its label for each year, and the components behind it (staff view).
fs16.publicNote: Public pages show the label only. Staff see the components behind each label when signed in. Security, safeguards and cyber roles appear at career-path level only and concept roles have no vacancy, so neither carries a label.
fs16.versionsDesc: When the criteria change, a new version is published; labels keep the version they were made under.

hr.title: This year's labels

hr.onlyDirector: Only the HR director can publish.
hr.confirmBody: {n} role labels are published ({changed} change). The labels are public; the components stay staff-only. This is audited and recorded in the NEXUS evidence ledger.

fs16.disclaimer: Labels are planning signals built from SIMULATED outlook inputs and FS05 planning assumptions. They are not forecasts, carry no staffing numbers and imply no deployment decision. ENEC decides roles and vacancies.

reason.growing: Growing: demand growth and shortfall both cross their thresholds
reason.changing: Changing: the 2030 profile change crosses its threshold
reason.stable: Stable: no signal crosses its threshold
reason.change: Profile change by 2030: {pct}% of today's requirement weight (threshold {min}%)
reason.change_none: No profile change measured for this role
reason.growth_none: Demand growth not available (families suppressed in the outlook)
reason.shortfall: Demand above holders in {year}: {pct}% of demand
reason.archived: Archived label: kept as it was published that year
reason.simulated: Inputs are SIMULATED planning numbers, not forecasts

fs34.privacy: The translation runs in your browser from published reference data. Kafa'a does not save your choice, does not ask who you are and sends nothing to anyone.
fs34.none: No source occupations are published yet

fig.uk: New nuclear jobs the UK plans by 2030

fs34.pickFirstBody: You will see the nearest ENEC roles, what transfers, the delta skills and the bridging route.
fs34.levelsNote: Levels are typical for an experienced practitioner (a template assumption, not a measurement of you). ESCO concepts read {date}.
fs34.resultsDesc: The {n} roles open to experienced entrants that your skills cover best, each with what transfers, what is missing and how to bridge it.
fs34.coverLine: Your skills cover {pct} of the role's requirements; {n} of {of} competencies already count.
fs34.noTransfers: Nothing counts yet: start with the cross-over course.
fs34.noGaps: No gap: you meet every requirement.
fs34.passportBody: The same rule, run on your own skill states instead of an occupation template. Your current role is left out; nothing is saved.
fs34.passportEmpty: Your skills passport has no skill states yet
fs34.heldN: Translated from {n} skills in your passport.

method.cover: Coverage is the Career Navigator formula: for each competency a role needs, the level you bring (up to the level needed) divided by the level needed, weighted core 3, important 2, useful 1.
method.roles: Only current roles open to experienced entrants (entry and professional levels) are proposed. Security, safeguards and cyber roles are shown at career-path level only and never here; concept future roles have no vacancy.
method.route: The route starts with the cross-over courses for your industry, then for each gap the shortest published course that teaches it (one level), then supervised practice at {per} hours per level left. Weeks assume {week} study hours a week.
method.templates: Each occupation is an ESCO v1.2 concept; every skill listed rests on an essential or optional ESCO skill of that occupation, marked exact when the Kafa'a crosswalk already aligns the two.
method.limits: This is guidance, not an offer or an assessment: it does not measure you, and entry still follows ENEC's recruitment and qualification rules. SMR content is concept learning; no deployment decision implied.

fs35.intro: Five visible parts of your career health, each with its inputs and rule, then a plan and a career conversation. There is no hidden score.
fs35.private: Your health check is never shown to your manager, HR or talent review. Only what you choose to write in a conversation request is shared.

stepHint.chart: Choose what you will do about the ones to watch or act on.

rule.recency: Months since your last completed learning. Good up to {good}, watch up to {watch}.
rule.mobility: Other current roles whose competencies you cover at {reach} or more. Good from {good}, watch from {watch}.
rule.change: Your readiness for your role's 2030 profile (Role in 2030). Good from {good}, watch from {watch}.
